> 无挂碍故，无有恐怖，远离一切颠倒梦想，究竟涅槃。

The chain is explicit here, and it is a chain of consequence rather than a list of virtues.

Because there is no obstruction, there is no fear.
Because there is no fear, the inverted dreams are left behind.
Because the inverted dreams are left behind, there is nirvana.

Each link is a function of the one before it. Fear does not get treated; it stops being generated. Dreams do not get interpreted; they stop being believed.

## Fear is a lease on something

The book's account: fear is born of 挂碍, of holding. Hold pleasure and you fear its loss. Hold the body as self and you fear its decay. Hold the project of improvement and you fear regression. Behind every fear there is an object of attachment, and the fear is simply that attachment seen from the side of loss.

This is why "let go of your fear" is useless advice. There is nothing to let go of directly; fear is a shadow cast by a grip. Remove the grip and the shadow has no object to fall on.

The sutra's wording is careful: 无有恐怖, no fear exists. Not: fear is conquered. Not: fear is felt but not acted upon. The claim is that with nothing held, the mechanism has no input.

## 颠倒梦想 is a bigger category than it sounds

颠倒: inverted — taking the unreal as real, the provisional as permanent, the borrowed as owned.

梦想: dream — and this is where the translation misleads almost everyone. In English, "dreams" suggests sleep, so the phrase reads as a comment about nighttime and gets filed away as poetic.

The book's gloss is much less comfortable: 梦想 covers everything the mind constructs and then treats as predictive — the plan for next quarter, the rehearsal of a conversation that has not happened, the memory replayed until it becomes a verdict, the dread of a diagnosis not yet received. All of it is 心念构画出来的影像 — images drawn by thought and then lived inside.

Not false in the sense of fictional. False in the sense of being constructed and then mistaken for given.

## 远离 does not mean leaving

The most likely misreading of the line is geographic: go somewhere quiet, close the senses, and the dreams cannot reach you.

The book refuses it. 远离 is not escape from circumstances and not the closing of the gates. It is the end of the inversion — the images still arise, and they are no longer believed. The room is as noisy as it was. The difference is that the noise no longer supplies a plot.

## 涅槃 as 息

And then 究竟涅槃, where another mistranslation waits. Nirvana read as a place — a deathless realm entered after death or after deep absorption — turns the whole sentence into a promise about the future.

The book takes the word at its root: 息, the stopping of fabrication driven by ignorance. Ordinary calm is 息 too, but it is a 息 within the cycle — quiet now, noisy later, with the alternation intact. 究竟 means the alternation itself has been seen through.

So nirvana is not a state you arrive at. It is what remains when the driving stops. Which is a much smaller claim than the tradition usually makes, and a much harder one to test, because there is no experience to check it against.

## The test

Name the fear you are carrying this week. Then name what it would cost you to lose. That second item is the grip.

Now the harder question: is the fear proportional to the object, or is the object there in order to give the fear somewhere to live?
